title: Personal Account Age and Pocketwire Advance Late Fee Relief
content:
For the payroll-delay relief on a Pocketwire Advance line, the age of the linked Pocketwire Personal Account is taken from its opening date. When the linked personal account was opened at least 1095 days before the handling date, 0.05 is added to the relief share; when it was opened at least 365 days but fewer than 1095 days before the handling date, 0.02 is added to the relief share; a younger personal account adds nothing to the relief share. The relief share is the fraction of the late fee that the relief returns.

The age is the number of calendar days from the opening date of the personal account to the handling date. It is read from the personal account's record, not from the Pocketwire Advance line's own opening date.

## Ages and what they add

| Personal account opened before the handling date | Added to the relief share |
|---|---|
| 1095 days or more | 0.05 |
| 365 to 1094 days | 0.02 |
| Fewer than 365 days | Nothing |

## Boundary pairs (hypothetical ages)

- Opened exactly 1095 days before the handling date: 0.05. Opened 1094 days before: 0.02.
- Opened exactly 365 days before the handling date: 0.02. Opened 364 days before: nothing.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A customer whose Pocketwire Personal Account was opened four years ago and whose Pocketwire Advance line was opened six months ago has a personal account well over 1095 days old, so 0.05 is added to the relief share; the younger age of the advance line plays no part here.
